sections.label: Traffic fatalities 2010 to 2020
sections.summary: Annual traffic fatalities fell from 193 in 2010 to 118 in 2019, then to 85 in 2020, partly due to COVID-19 and less traffic.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of Home Affairs)
sentences.text: From 2010 to 2019, the annual number of traffic fatalities has dropped by close to 40% from 193 fatalities in 2010 to 118 fatalities in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The number of fatalities decreased further to 85 in 2020, although this was partly due to the COVID-19 situation when there was less traffic, especially during the circuit breaker period.

sections.label: Illegal speed trials penalties
sections.summary: From 2018 to 2020, TP arrested 31 persons for illegal speed trials, and clause 22 increases maximum jail terms and fines for these offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of Home Affairs)
sentences.text: From 2018 to 2020, TP arrested 31 persons for illegal speed trials.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To increase deterrence, clause 22 increases the maximum jail terms and fines for taking part in or promoting illegal speed trials.

sections.label: Conspiring to mislead authorities offence
sections.summary: Clause 20 creates a new offence for individuals who conspire to mislead the authorities, with higher maximum jail terms and fines than the existing false information offence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 20 creates a new offence aimed at individuals who conspire to mislead the authorities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The maximum jail terms and fines for these offences will be higher than the penalties for the existing offence of wilfully or recklessly furnishing false or misleading information.

sections.label: Expanding section 42 offence list
sections.summary: Clause 13 expands the list of offences in section 42 to include any offence under any written law instead of a list of prescribed Penal Code offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clause 13 expands the list of offences in section 42 to include any offence under any written law instead of limiting the provision to a list of prescribed Penal Code offences.

sections.label: PAB riding without theory test
sections.summary: The new section 47G makes it an offence to ride a PAB on any road without having passed the theory test.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The new section 47G makes it an offence to ride a PAB on any road without having passed the theory test.

sections.label: Obsolete provision and Bill purpose
sections.summary: This provision is obsolete as TP no longer issues on-the-spot tickets and compounds all traffic offences not prosecuted in Court, and the Bill aims to make roads safer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This provision is obsolete, as TP no longer issues on-the-spot tickets and compounds all traffic offences that are not prosecuted in Court.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister of Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This Bill is necessary to help make our roads even safer, by enhancing our measures against irresponsible behaviour and enacting the regulations for PAB riders.

sections.label: Fatal accidents motorcyclists elderly pedestrians
sections.summary: Motorcyclists were in over 63% of 2020 fatal accidents, and half of fatal accidents involving elderly pedestrians were due to jaywalking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Motorcyclists were involved in more than 63% of fatal accidents in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Half of the fatal accidents involving elderly pedestrians were due to jaywalking.

sections.label: Vehicular fires per year
sections.summary: The Minister said there are 200 vehicular fires yearly, but the cause is difficult to pinpoint in most incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The hon Minister informed that there are 200 vehicular fires per year but for the majority of the fire incidents, it would be difficult to pinpoint the cause of the fire.

sections.label: PAB pillion rider age
sections.summary: Pillion riders on PABs must be at least 16 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In comparison, pillion riders on PABs must be at least 16 years old.

sections.label: Section 117(7) vehicle forfeiture
sections.summary: Proposed section 117(7) makes forfeiture non-mandatory where a non-owner used the vehicle without the owner's consent for speed trials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: My question concerns the proposed section 117(7) of the Road Traffic Act which makes the vehicle forfeiture regime non-mandatory where such vehicles are used for speed trials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It is stated in the provision that the Court "need not" make an order for forfeiture where the person who committed the offence is not the owner of the vehicle and he used it without the consent of the owner.

sections.label: Section 81 vehicle usage records
sections.summary: Proposed section 81 makes company, partnership or unincorporated body owners keep vehicle usage records, with personal responsibility on chairperson, managing director or company secretary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the proposed section 81, where the owner of the vehicle is a company, a partnership or an unincorporated body, it is the owner's responsibility to keep a proper record of the vehicle's usage and the persons driving the vehicle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The personal responsibility is reposed on the chairperson, managing director or the company secretary of a company or positions analogous to any of these offices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: What is the rationale of making the chairperson, managing director or company secretary personally responsible for maintaining a proper record of a vehicle usage?

sections.label: Clause 22 illegal racing penalties
sections.summary: Clause 22 increases penalties for conducting illegal competitions or trials of speed involving vehicles, or racing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 22 of this Bill will increase the penalties for the offence of conducting illegal competitions or trials of speed involving vehicles, in short, racing.

sections.label: Illegal racing penalties increased
sections.summary: The Bill proposes to double the maximum imprisonment and more than double the maximum fines for illegal racing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I have been liaising with TP and LTA for several months over such threats to public safety.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Bill proposes to significantly increase the punishment for the offence of illegal racing, by doubling the maximum imprisonment and more than doubling the maximum fines.

sections.label: Clause 20 maximum fine raised
sections.summary: Clause 20 proposes to increase the punishment for this offence, raising the maximum fine to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 20 also proposes to increase the punishment for this offence, in particular, the maximum fine.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is now proposed to raise the maximum fine to $10,000.

sections.label: Frisk searches by approved persons
sections.summary: The Bill proposes frisk searches by Police officers and senior approved persons, including Auxiliary Police, security officers and outsourced enforcement officers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes that frisk searches may be conducted by Police officers and those defined as “senior approved persons”. “Senior approved persons” are, in turn, defined to include members of the Auxiliary Police, security officers engaged by the public transport operator, and outsourced enforcement officers.

sections.label: Special Events Security search powers
sections.summary: Part III of the Public Order Act reserves search powers at special event areas to SPF officers, while others do less-intrusive checks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the Public Order Act, Part III on Special Events Security reserves the power to search persons entering a special event area to SPF officers only; others, such as Auxiliary Police and private security are empowered to do less-intrusive forms of security checks, such as checking bags and manning scanners.

sections.label: Identification declaration and production
sections.summary: Clauses 24 and 31 require plainclothes Police officers or approved persons to declare their office before compliance, with only outsourced enforcement officers producing identification cards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clauses 24 and 31 provide that a Police officer in plainclothes or an approved person must declare his office to the person before he or she is required to comply.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The only category of officers who are required to produce identification cards to the public are outsourced enforcement officers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This Bill seems to be a lowering of the standards set by the Road Traffic Act itself, as section 128 of the Act currently requires Police officers not in uniform to produce their identification card to the public when asked.

sections.label: Test handbooks and language availability
sections.summary: LTA's website states handbooks are in English and will be translated into Chinese, Malay and Tamil, and the Member asks about notices and tests in those languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: LTA’s website states that the handbooks for the tests are currently available in English and will, subsequently, be translated into Chinese, Malay and Tamil.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share if the notices to inform existing riders of the need to take these tests will also be delivered in multiple languages, so that non-English speaking riders will be fully aware of this development and not be blindsided because of a language barrier?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister of State also share if the test itself will be available in Chinese, Malay and Tamil?

sections.label: PMD and PAB test fees
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether test fees will be kept low or subsidised for lower-income PMD and PAB riders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share if the test fees will be kept low or whether the Ministry has plans to subsidise test fees for PMD and PAB riders who fall below a certain income bracket, to ensure that this test does not pose an additional burden on them?

sections.label: Competency test certificate requirement
sections.summary: The Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill introduces a competency test certificate requirement for riding a road-only power-assisted bicycle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill is introducing, among other things, the requirement of a competency test certificate for a rider to ride only a road-only power-assisted bicycle (PAB).

sections.label: Certification cost and financial assistance
sections.summary: A speaker hopes certification course fees are kept low, financial assistance is available, and renewals are not too regular.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Some people have cited the cost of requiring certification as a cause of concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government will ensure that the certification course and associated course fees are kept low at all times and that those who cannot afford the fees can receive financial assistance for these fees so that they are still able to use such forms of transport and that there should not be too regular renewals.

sections.label: Cycling culture and enforcement resources
sections.summary: The speaker says improving cycling culture needs political will, recalling past complaints about non-enforcement and authorities citing inadequate resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I also said that, to improve our cycling culture, the Government must have the political will to do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I then reflected that around 10 years before that, I remember there was at one time a flurry of complaints in the newspapers about non-enforcement against errant cyclists, cyclists cycling on the wrong side of the road or beating red lights were already common occurrences then.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: I remember once the authorities replied to say that they had inadequate resources to address the problem.

sections.label: Consistent enforcement and public education
sections.summary: The speaker says he has repeatedly raised the need for consistent enforcement and adequate public education to improve riding culture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: In my speech for the Active Mobility Bill debate in 2017 and on numerous subsequent occasions in Parliament over the past few years, I have harped on the need to work on having consistent enforcement and adequate public education in order to improve our riding culture, whether for e-scooters, e-bikes or bicycles.

sections.label: Enforcement and education beyond spot-checks
sections.summary: The speaker says consistent enforcement must go beyond spot-checks and public education beyond safe riding courses or online publicity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: As I have said on numerous occasions previously, consistent enforcement must go beyond occasional or even weekly spot-checks in selected spots and public education must go beyond just safe riding courses or online publicity to educate those who do not solicit the information by themselves.

sections.label: Cycling culture and active mobility
sections.summary: The passage argues that getting riding culture right is needed if cycling and active mobility are to be taken seriously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If this is considered to be too difficult, we should not be surprised, as we did not do it earlier when we had fewer categories of cyclists and with less busy roads, no busy connector or footpath networks used by different types of users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: And we should not be half-hearted about this if we have invested huge resources for cycling in our extended cycling network and have nice plans for cycling lanes elsewhere, if we intend to take cycling and other forms of active mobility seriously, and if we still believe in active mobility for last-mile connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: If the LTA still harbours any wish for e-scooters to make a return as a choice transport for last-mile connectivity, we had better get our riding culture right, right now.

sections.label: Regulatory sandbox extension to 2027
sections.summary: The Bill proposes extending the regulatory sandbox for another five years, until 2027, to facilitate more trials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Bill proposes to extend this regulatory sandbox for another five years, to facilitate even more trials until 2027.

sections.label: Cyclists and bus lanes
sections.summary: The passage urges the Ministry not to allow cyclists and PAB users on bus lanes during operational hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: It is also common for buses to have to overtake and re-overtake the same peloton of cyclists, as they bypass the bus at bus stops; and the dangerous cycle – pardon the pun – repeats itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to not allow cyclists and PAB users on bus lanes during operational hours.

sections.label: Separate transport for workers
sections.summary: The Labour Movement is engaging SCAL to push for separate transport arrangements for workers as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement is engaging the Singapore Contractors Association Limited, or SCAL, to push for the implementation of separate transport arrangements for workers as soon as possible.

sections.label: Banning goods and passenger co-mingling
sections.summary: The passage states that the co-mingling of goods and passengers should be outlawed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Second, the co-mingling of goods and passengers should be outlawed.

sections.label: Lorry accident injury risk
sections.summary: The passage states that while lorry accidents may have fallen over 10 years, the risk of major injury or fatality per incident is high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: While the number of accidents involving lorries may have gone down over the past 10 years, the risk for major injury and fatality per incident is high.

sections.label: Cargo area passenger safety
sections.summary: A research paper suggests cargo area passengers are 7.9 times more likely to die in accidents, and measures to offset employer costs are proposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: One research paper suggests that passengers in cargo areas are 7.9 times more likely to lose their lives in the event of an accident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I hope the Government can help offset the financial burden employers will face when enhancing the transportation safety for our workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We could exempt buses used to transport our workers from COE, similar to how school buses are already exempted today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We could also provide an early adopter grant to incentivise employers to purchase or lease buses to transport their workers.

sections.label: Safe Riding Programme revamp
sections.summary: LTA has offered the free voluntary Safe Riding Programme since 2018 and will roll out a revamped version in the next few months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Since 2018, LTA has offered the Safe Riding Programme (SRP).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: This is a voluntary education programme that is free-of-charge with both theory and practical components for all active mobility device users, including cyclists.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: LTA is revamping the SRP and will work with Traffic Police to reach out to road users and encourage public participation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We intend to roll out the new Safe Riding Programme in the next few months." Sir, I wanted also to clarify what Mr Dennis Tan said earlier about how four years ago he has been raising Parliamentary Questions on riding culture.

sections.label: Cyclist and PAB accidents
sections.summary: LTA reported 417 road accidents involving cyclists and PAB users from January to November 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to LTA, there were 417 road accidents involving cyclists and PAB users from January to November 2019.

sections.label: Two accidents kill two men
sections.summary: In two weeks, two accidents killed 28-year-old Mr Sugunan Sudheeshmon from Kerala and 33-year-old Mr Tofazzal Hossain from Bangladesh.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a span of two weeks, two accidents claimed the lives of two young men – 28-year-old Mr Sugunan Sudheeshmon from Kerala and 33-year-old Mr Tofazzal Hossain from Bangladesh.

sections.label: Traffic Police accident figures
sections.summary: Traffic Police reported three deaths and 244 injuries in similar accidents last year, in only the first half of the year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the Traffic Police, three people died and 244 people were injured in similar accidents last year and, for us, it is only the first half of the year.

sections.label: Lorries and seatbelt forces
sections.summary: Senior Minister of State Amy Khor said lorries are not built to withstand the forces needed to hold seatbelts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Earlier on, Senior Minister of State Amy Khor had said that the lorries are not built to withstand the forces needed to hold the seatbelts.

sections.label: Truck transport and PAB rider licensing
sections.summary: The speaker raises truck transport safety, welcomes a review, supports the Bill, and notes the Bill requires certification for power-assisted bicycle riders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Additionally, after a long day of work, workers on trucks may also fall asleep and, while being transported in such a state, it will be difficult for them to react to cushion any major movements made by the lorry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similar to what fellow Member of Parliament Mr Alex Yam brought up about SAF having seat belts for their five-tonners yesterday, should we revisit the discussion on how SAF has been transporting their men and how we can adapt such measures to these cases?

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I welcome the announcement that there will be a review on this issue with all the relevant stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding what I have asked to be considered, on the whole, I feel this Bill protects the lives of everyone on the road and, for that, I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A major focus of the Bill is the licensing and certification of riders of “test-needed-to-ride-on-road vehicles”.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: These are power-assisted bicycles (PABs) that are prescribed by the rules under the Active Mobility Act 2017, and the new rules require that riders of such vehicles be certified to have passed a prescribed test of competence for that class or description of vehicle and the test of competence will cover riding on public paths and roads.

sections.label: Migrant worker lorry accidents
sections.summary: Last month two migrant workers died and scores were injured in lorry accidents, with about 300,000 such workers facing dangerous daily commutes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Just last month, two migrant workers lost their lives and scores more were injured in a series of accidents involving lorries, and there was one just a few days ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given that there are approximately 300,000 such workers in Singapore, this is a large number of our population who face dangerous commutes on a daily basis.

sections.label: Road Traffic Act goods vehicle ban
sections.summary: Section 126 of the Road Traffic Act bans carrying passengers in goods vehicles, except employees on the owner's business or sick or injured persons in emergencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, section 126 of the Road Traffic Act still has a provision banning the use of goods vehicles for passengers, unless, I quote, "(a) the person so carried is in the employment of the owner or hirer of the vehicle and is proceeding on his master's business and is carried in accordance with rules prescribed under section 77(6); or (b) the person so carried is a sick or injured person carried in a case of emergency".

sections.label: Small bus owners funding
sections.summary: The Government set aside $35 million to help owners of small buses implement this.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A sum of $35 million was set aside by the Government to help owners of small buses implement this.

sections.label: Mandating buses for migrant workers
sections.summary: The speaker asks why Singapore cannot learn from other countries and says it must seriously consider mandating buses or mini-buses for all migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Why can we not learn from them how these countries address the very same concerns that we have, while at the same time mandating that workers are transported in a safer manner?

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must seriously consider mandating that all migrant workers are transported in buses or mini-buses.

sections.label: Study of transport safety costs
sections.summary: The speaker calls for a proper study of costs and the construction labour model, rather than vague statements about costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: In any event, we should also have a proper study of the costs – both as an absolute number across the industry and as a percentage of total construction costs – associated with enhancing safety measures for the transport of our migrant workers, together with a good look at the labour model for our construction industry in order to have a more meaningful conversation on this topic, rather than have vague statements being made about costs each time the topic is brought up.

sections.label: Female authorised persons frisk searching women
sections.summary: It suggests mandating that only female authorised persons may frisk search other women, given expanded frisk search powers.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For example, in view of the expansion of powers to include frisk searching, we could, as earlier suggested, mandate that only female authorised persons are allowed to frisk search other women.

sections.label: Repeal of worker transport provision
sections.summary: It proposes repealing section 126(1)(a) and mandating passenger seats for worker transport, while the Minister urged studying existing lorry safety measures first.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What steps will need to be taken to ensure that this does not happen?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I propose to add a provision to the Bill to repeal section 126(1)(a) of the Act and to mandate that workers can only be transported in vehicles with passenger seats.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Minister replied that we should allow the measures to improve workers’ safety on lorries to take effect and study their effectiveness before concluding that they are insufficient and going for a ban.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These measures – fitting lorries with canopies and side railings, increasing the deck space per seated worker – have been in place for 10 years.

sections.label: Financial assistance for small bus retrofits
sections.summary: The Government gave $22 million in financial assistance for small buses to be retrofitted with seat belts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To cope with the increased cost, the Government gave out $22 million in financial assistance for small buses to be retrofitted with seat belts.

sections.label: MOT review of issue
sections.summary: It states the pandemic shows the easier or cheaper path can backfire, and MOT will review the issue considering all views and suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The pandemic has shown us how choosing the easier or cheaper path can come back and bite us eventually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It was announced yesterday that MOT will review this issue, taking into account all views and suggestions.

sections.label: PAB rider competency test requirement
sections.summary: The amendment requires PAB riders to pass a competency test and obtain a certificate, with some vocational riders citing language or technology barriers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendment seeks to require PAB riders to undergo a competency test and to be granted a certificate before riding the vehicle on the road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A proportion of vocational PAB riders, such as food delivery riders, have shared their concerns with us that they will find it challenging to pass the theory test due to language or technology barriers.

sections.label: Timeline for PAB rider certification
sections.summary: It states the Bill's changes should be implemented with a reasonable timeline giving vocational PAB riders adequate runway to get certification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The changes arising from the passing of the Bill should be implemented with a reasonable timeline, providing vocational PAB riders an adequate runway to get their certification.

sections.label: Delivery platforms' duty to freelancers
sections.summary: A request for MOM to clarify delivery platforms' duty to freelance and self-employed workers under the Workplace Safety and Health Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, we have many freelance and self-employed workers who work for various delivery platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would like MOM to clarify the duty of these delivery platforms towards their freelance and self-employed workers under the Workplace Safety and Health Act.

sections.label: Power-assisted bicycle theory test
sections.summary: Proposed Road Traffic Act amendments would require power-assisted bicycle riders to pass a theory test before riding on roads or pavements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to the Road Traffic Act would require power-assisted bicycle riders to pass a theory test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is before they can ride their power-assisted bicycles on the roads or on the pavements.

sections.label: Converting roads to cycling lanes
sections.summary: Authorities swiftly created many new cycling lanes within months by converting about 150 kilometres of roads to cycling lanes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Yet, the authorities were able to swiftly create many new cycling lanes within months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: They accomplished this by converting about 150 kilometres of roads to cycling lanes.

sections.label: Cyclist theory test recommendation
sections.summary: A recommendation is for cyclists to take a theory test like a CPR qualification before going on the roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Another recommendation is for cyclists to take a theory test like a CPR qualification before they can go on the roads.

sections.label: Causation-based accident liability
sections.summary: Simplifying fault determination by causation could make road users more self-aware, reduce reckless behaviour and make roads safer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What this means is that even if it was possible for the motorist to show that it was the cyclist that caused the accident, the motorist would find it a lot more difficult to show that they have not breached their duty of care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What if liability for a traffic accident involving a cyclist can be decided simply by causation?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Simplifying how fault is determined in a traffic accident could lead to road users becoming more self-aware of their own conduct on the roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This can reduce reckless behaviour and make roads safer for everyone.

sections.label: Licensing bicycle users
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to introduce licensing and certification regimes for users of bicycles and power-assisted bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Bill seeks to introduce licensing and certification regimes for users of bicycles and power-assisted bicycles.

sections.label: Roads to cycling paths
sections.summary: LTA has started looking into converting some road stretches into cycling paths to triple the Cycling Path Network by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: LTA has already started looking into converting some stretches of roads into cycling paths to tripling the Cycling Path Network by 2030.

sections.label: Disabled cyclists and cycling
sections.summary: For persons with disabilities, cycling is often easier than walking, and about 40% of disabled cyclists use regular two-wheeled bicycles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For persons with disabilities, cycling is often a much easier way to get around than walking and it is estimated that about 40% of disabled cyclists use regular two-wheeled bicycles.

sections.label: Publishing frisk search statistics
sections.summary: The Ministry may consider publishing statistics on all frisk searches, including gender, ethnicity, time, location and justification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Perhaps the Ministry may consider publishing statistics pertaining to all frisk searches, including information on searches by gender, ethnicity, time, location and also justification.

sections.label: Trust and public transport safety
sections.summary: This would help maintain trust in law enforcement while remaining vigilant against threats to public transport, boosting safety for riders and other road users.

sentences.speaker: Ms Raeesah Khan (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This would help maintain trust in law enforcement while allowing us to remain vigilant against potential threats to our public transport system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This will help boost safety for the riders and other users on the roads.

sections.label: Helmets for pillion riders
sections.summary: It will be a new offence for motorcyclists to carry pillion riders who are not wearing helmets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Next, it will be a new offence for motorcyclists to carry pillion riders who are not wearing helmets.

sections.label: Security screening of commuters
sections.summary: An amendment of the Bill empowers Police officers and authorised personnel to conduct security screening of bus and MRT commuters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Another amendment of the Bill is to empower Police officers and authorised personnel to conduct security screening of bus and MRT commuters.

sections.label: Vehicle forfeiture amendment
sections.summary: The amendment stops forfeiture of a vehicle if the offending driver is not the owner and used it without permission.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With the amendment, a vehicle involved will no longer be forfeited if the offending driver is not the owner and had used it without the owner's permission.

sections.label: Illegal street racing arrests
sections.summary: From 2018 to 2020, 31 people were arrested over four illegal street racing cases, and 57 motorists were investigated in a Tuas race.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: From 2018 to 2020, a total of 31 people have been arrested over four cases of illegal street racing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In a separate incident, also during the circuit breaker period, 57 motorists in 50 vehicles were investigated for taking part in an illegal car race in Tuas.

sections.label: Open face helmet testing prices
sections.summary: SMCTA states testing open face helmets costs S$1,283 for a minimum of four pieces, with the next five pieces at S$194 each.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: According to the Singapore Motor Cycle Trade Association (SMCTA), the price of testing open face helmets is S$1,283 for a minimum of four pieces, with the next five pieces costing S$194 each.

sections.label: Proposed helmet testing solutions
sections.summary: Proposed solutions include accepting ECE and SNELL standards, testing once per model, and making testing free or highly subsidised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In addition to considering accepting ECE and SNELL standards, some other proposed solution could be conducting the destructive test once per model rather than per batch and possibly making the testing free or at a highly subsidised rate to ensure affordability and, hence, enhance the safety of riders.

sections.label: Branded helmet safety standards
sections.summary: The speaker hopes MHA will consider other internationally accepted safety standards for branded helmets from well-known manufacturers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As such, for these branded helmets, I hope MHA can consider other internationally accepted safety standards, especially for helmets from well-known manufacturers.

sections.label: PAB test affordability
sections.summary: The question asks whether the PAB test can be made more affordable for those who rely on it to earn a living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Can we make the PAB test more affordable for those who rely on it to earn their living?

sections.label: Helmet standards and PAB theory test
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry to consider approving ECE and SNELL helmet standards and to ensure the mandatory PAB theory test does not affect riders' livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is also important to enforce basic safety standards for helmets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, I hope that the Ministry can consider approving other internationally accepted standards like ECE and SNELL so that our riders can equip themselves with safety gears that meet the international standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With regard to the mandatory theory test for PAB riders, we need to ensure that rolling it out does not affect the livelihood of many who are now dependent on the PAB.

sections.label: Updated penalties for illegal speed trials
sections.summary: The passage states first-offence penalties are a $5,000 fine and 12 months' imprisonment, five times the fine and double the sentence, hoping to deter illegal speed trials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The updated penalties are significant with the first offence carrying a fine of $5,000 and 12 months' imprisonment, making the monetary impact five times higher and doubling the prison sentence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Given the uptick in illegal speed trials in recent years, as mentioned by the Minister of State, it will, hopefully, deter and prevent needless loss of precious lives and damage to property, such as the devastating Tanjong Pagar car crash that happened a few months ago.

sections.label: Illegal modifications proportion
sections.summary: The passage states that 54 of these cases, over three quarters, relate to illegal modifications, which is a very high proportion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Of these, 54, or over three quarters, relate to illegal modifications and this is a very high proportion.

sections.label: Workshop charged over illegal modifications
sections.summary: The passage states that last week CNA reported a workshop was charged with three counts of illegal vehicle modifications under the RTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, last week, CNA reported that a workshop was charged with three counts of illegal vehicle modifications under the RTA.

sections.label: Instalment payments for traffic fines
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to make instalment payments more readily available for traffic fines, and notes a mandatory theory test regime for PAB users is among the amendments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A number of my residents who have not been able to have their traffic fines waived because of the seriousness of their offences, such as beating a red light or speeding, have often appealed to be given the option to pay the fine in instalments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope the Minister will consider making instalment payments more readily available so that they can pay fines without being put in a difficult financial position, which is not the objective of the RTA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One of the amendments is the introduction of a mandatory theory test regime for users of PABs.

sections.label: Rider code of conduct and online test
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the code of conduct would require riders to assist the other party in an accident, and notes the multiple-choice test will be conducted online.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Would the code of conduct require riders to render assistance to the other party in the event of an unfortunate accident?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It has been announced that the test, comprising multiple-choice questions, will be conducted online.

sections.label: Rider insurance and PAB tagging
sections.summary: Companies employing riders on public paths must provide third-party liability insurance, and enforcement may use technology to tag PABs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Companies which employ riders who use active mobility devices on public paths are required to cover them with third-party liability insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Lastly, enforcement will always be needed to ensure compliance and one of the ways is to utilise technology to tag the PABs.

sections.label: Road Traffic Act rider test
sections.summary: The amendments to the Road Traffic Act require these riders to pass a similar test before riding on the road.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The amendments to the Road Traffic Act introduce the need for these riders to pass a similar test before they can ride on the road.

sections.label: PAB handbook language and access
sections.summary: The PAB mandatory theory test handbook on the LTA website is only in English, and the Member asks about translating it and offline access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On to my next point, Mr Speaker, Sir, and this had been surfaced by many other Members in the Chamber.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that the official handbook for the PAB mandatory theory test that is available on the LTA website comes only in English.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Given that not all PAB riders are comfortable in English and are Internet-savvy, would there be plans to translate the current English handbook into other languages – such as Mandarin, Malay, Tamil, perhaps – and also make the handbook accessible to PAB riders offline as well?

sections.label: Ensuring all PAB riders tested
sections.summary: A qualifying test will enhance riders' road safety awareness, but the challenge is ensuring all PAB riders go through it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A final point, Mr Speaker, Sir, that I would like to raise was previously highlighted when I spoke about the Active Mobility (Amendment) Bill last year and, that is, while the implementation of a qualifying test will certainly enhance the riders' awareness of road safety, the challenge is in ensuring that all PAB riders will go through this test.

sections.label: Singapore AV readiness ranking
sections.summary: Singapore has been ranked first in the KPMG 2020 Autonomous Vehicles Readiness Index.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore has been ranked first in the KPMG 2020 Autonomous Vehicles Readiness Index.

sections.label: Extending AV sandbox five years
sections.summary: As the AV race becomes more competitive, the sandbox should be extended by another five years for AV technology to mature and be fully tested.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: However, the AV race will become more competitive as more AV companies enter the market and make breakthroughs in AV technology.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Therefore, we should extend the sandbox by another five years for the AV technology to be more mature and fully tested.

sections.label: Road traffic rules insurance changes
sections.summary: MOT and the law enforcement and insurance fraternities must work out corresponding changes in road traffic rules, insurance coverage and compensation framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: MOT, the law enforcement and insurance fraternities must also work out the corresponding changes needed in the road traffic rules, insurance coverage and compensation framework.

sections.label: AVs five to 10 years
sections.summary: The speaker assures that AVs will not happen overnight, leaving five to 10 years to prepare for socio-economic disruption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: At this point, I can only assure them that AVs will not happen overnight.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We will still have another five to 10 years to avert this disruptive socio-economic impact and we must make good use of this window to prepare ourselves well for this socio-economic disruption.

sections.label: Competency certificate requirement timing
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry to clarify when the competency certificate requirement will take place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry clarify when the requirement for the competency certificate will take place?

sections.label: Transition period before theory test
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry could consider a transition period before the theory test requirement to ride on the road is effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: To not unduly penalise these workers, could the Ministry consider a transition period before the theory test requirement to ride on the road is effective?

sections.label: Section 47K platform companies
sections.summary: The passage asks for confirmation that section 47K also applies to platform companies that engage and allow untested riders on the roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can I clarify and confirm that section 47K also applies to platform companies, such as the food delivery companies, which engage and allow untested riders on the roads?

sections.label: Platform companies internalise theory test costs
sections.summary: The passage calls on platform companies to internalise the costs of the theory tests for their delivery riders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Additionally, I would like to call on platform companies to internalise the costs of the theory tests for their delivery riders.

sections.label: PAB rider database and liability
sections.summary: A database would ease transport companies' compliance and help ensure only competent PAB riders are on roads, with stakeholders sharing legal liabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: To ease transport companies' compliance to the new certificate requirements and perhaps reduce prosecution under section 47K, a database would go a long way towards ensuring that only competent PAB riders are allowed on the roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Stakeholders who play a significant role in contributing and benefiting from safe deliveries and road usage must similarly also share in the corresponding legal liabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Holding them liable and magnifying their role in road safety reflect their growing importance.

sections.label: PAB combined theory test support
sections.summary: The pandemic increased cycling, PAB and e-scooter use, and the speaker supports the combined theory test regime for PABs on roads and shared paths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The pandemic led to a boom in cycling, power-assisted bicycles (PABs) and e-scooter usage has increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am supportive of the combined theory test regime for the use of PABs on roads and shared paths.

sections.label: AV sandbox extension support
sections.summary: Safety issues must be ironed out before mass deployment, and the speaker supports extending AV regulatory sandboxes due to expire in 2022 by five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is essential that safety issues are ironed out properly ahead of any mass deployment in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am supportive that the AV regulatory sandboxes which are due to expire in 2022 will be extended by another five years to facilitate trials and deployments.

sections.label: Graduated self-driving certification approach
sections.summary: The speaker hopes for standard tests and asks about a graduated certification approach, noting a fatal Tesla crash reignited debate on self-driving safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I hope this extension and eventual deployment will allow a set of standard tests and make companies benchmark their algorithms on standard datasets before their vehicles are allowed on open roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It may still be in early stages, but will there be a graduated approach to certification in which a self-driving system could first be evaluated in simulations, then in controlled real-world environments, pass specific benchmark tests before they can be allowed on open roads?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The recent crash of a Tesla car in the United States in which two people died has reignited debate about the capabilities and safety of today's self-driving technologies.

sections.label: PAB riders' safety and livelihoods
sections.summary: The Government is commended for measures ensuring PAB riders' safety, with mandatory theory tests as a first step for their lives and livelihoods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Even as they ride to put food on our tables, we must make sure that they get home safely to put food on their tables as well.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It is commendable that the Government is taking measures to ensure the safety of PAB riders even if the first step towards securing their lives and livelihoods takes the form of mandatory theory tests.

sections.label: Delivery rider rules and cycling paths
sections.summary: The speaker calls for reviewing food delivery platforms' rewards and punitive actions, and for flexibility in the PAB test handbook amid expanding cycling infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Surely, Mr Speaker, the rules of the game must be changed to complement the education of our delivery riders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, we call for a review of the rewards and punitive actions run by food delivery platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Singapore now boasts 460 kilometres of cycling paths, with plans to triple and expand the density of our cycling network to 1,300 kilometres by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Should the PAB theory test define the rules of the road for riders, we must also maintain a flexibility in the test handbook to accommodate for the ever-evolving face of road infrastructure in Singapore in a bid to promote active mobility.

sections.label: PAB safety and online test
sections.summary: Speaker thanks authorities for PAB safety measures and asks for lower test fees and translated or audio test versions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):    First of all, let me thank the authorities again for introducing appropriate measures to ensure that PABs are used safely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This Bill not only provides for the safety of riders, but also pedestrians and other road users.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The convenience brought about by the one-off online test will help many people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, we must consider carefully if we can lower the test fee and provide translated or audio versions of the online test for users with different needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: These considerations are essential, because this will ensure that riders of different language abilities can take the test equally and that riders with different education qualifications can all take part.

sections.label: Sandbox extension for AV trials
sections.summary: Clause 3 of the Bill extends the sandbox permitting AV trials from 2022 to 2027.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Specifically, clause 3 of the Bill extends the sandbox that permits the AV trials from 2022 to 2027.

sections.label: Five-year AV sandbox extension
sections.summary: Extending the sandbox until August 2027 lets companies develop and trial AV technology in Punggol, Tengah and Jurong Innovation District.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: However, fully autonomous transport remains a long-term aspiration, requiring more R&D.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Therefore, extending the sandbox by five years until August 2027 will allow these companies to continue to develop and trial AV technology for local deployment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As previously announced, this will take place in Punggol, Tengah and the Jurong Innovation District, under the Call-for-Collaboration launched by LTA.

sections.label: LTA bus captain upskilling MOU
sections.summary: In 2019 LTA signed a Memorandum of Understanding with industry stakeholders to upskill public bus captains.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: In 2019, to demonstrate our commitment to upskill our public bus captains, LTA signed a Memorandum of Understanding with industry stakeholders, including the public transport operators and the National Transport Workers’ Union.

sections.label: New standards and ambulance tax exemption
sections.summary: From 1 September this year, some vehicles may no longer function as ambulances and so no longer qualify for tax exemption.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: When these new standards take effect from 1 September this year, some vehicles might no longer be able to function as ambulances and, hence, will no longer qualify for tax exemption.

sections.label: Female officers conduct frisk searches
sections.summary: Only authorised female officers can conduct frisk searches on a female person, to safeguard modesty and ensure professionalism.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: To safeguard the modesty of a female person and to ensure frisk searches are conducted professionally, only authorised female officers can conduct frisk searches on a female person.

sections.label: Higher composition sum and vehicle detention
sections.summary: LTA will double the composition sum to $1,000 for new offences from 1 July and seek court detention of repeat offenders' vehicles up to three months.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Going forward, LTA will double the composition sum to $1,000 for new offences committed from 1 July this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Furthermore, for repeat offenders, LTA will apply to the Court to detain the offending vehicle for up to three months.

sections.label: Single theory test for PAB riders
sections.summary: The RTA amendments will enable a single theory test for PAB riders on roads and cycling paths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: The amendments to the RTA today will enable us to implement a single theory test for PAB riders on roads and cycling paths.

sections.label: Test charge for first three months
sections.summary: For the first three months, the test will be chargeable at $5 for two attempts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: For the first three months, the test will be chargeable at $5 for two attempts.

sections.label: Subsequent test charge per attempt
sections.summary: Subsequently, the test will be chargeable at $10 for each attempt.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Subsequently, the test will be chargeable at $10 for each attempt.

sections.label: Offence for uncertified rider
sections.summary: It will be an offence for a company to allow an uncertified rider on the road with knowledge or negligence as to certification.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Yes, it will be an offence for a company to allow an uncertified rider to ride on the road with the knowledge that the rider is uncertified or being negligent as to whether the rider is uncertified.

sections.label: Lorry accidents and declining casualty rate
sections.summary: The speaker is saddened by recent lorry accidents but notes injury and fatality rates for persons onboard lorries fell over the last decade amid measures like side railings and canopies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: As I mentioned yesterday, we are deeply saddened by the recent accidents involving lorries ferrying workers and understand the concerns raised by Members.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: However, we also cannot just ignore the fact that the injury and fatality rate involving persons onboard lorries has come down over the last decade, as various measures, such as side railings and canopies, enhanced test requirements for drivers, sustained engagement and enforcement, have been implemented.

sections.label: Regulatory changes and COVID-19 industry pain
sections.summary: Regulatory changes now would cause more acute pain to an industry already severely affected by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Regulatory changes now will cause even more acute pain to the industry, given that the industry is being severely affected by COVID-19.

sections.label: Migrant workers and safety rules review
sections.summary: Safety rules will be reviewed with stakeholders to find a balanced way forward for the benefit of all.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: And for the migrant workers, this is the very reason why they are here.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: We will continue to review the existing safety rules, engage stakeholders along the way, taking all feedback and suggestions, as I have said, and find a sensible and balanced way forward, taking into account all concerns for the benefit of all.

sections.label: LTA notices of offence
sections.summary: Between January and April this year, LTA issued 227 notices of offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
sentences.text: Between January and April this year, LTA had issued 227 notices of offence.

sections.label: Safeguards, authorised officers and security checks
sections.summary: Safeguards are recorded in Hansard, only trained authorised officers conduct checks, and security checks match those for major public events.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, while these safeguards are recorded in the Hansard, would that also be enshrined in some subsidiary legislation or made public in an easy-to-understand form so that commuters as well as the officers empowered to search would know where the boundaries lie?

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: But it is only authorised officers who have gone through the approved training, and this will be the Police officers, the auxiliary officers, the security officers, enforcement officers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: If the Police is not in uniform, then they will have to identify themselves.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: And it also depends on the alert level, the threat level.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: I do not have the name with me, it is in a file back there, because I thought we are going to have the Minister of State's speech before we have clarifications, but I can give it to you.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: It is actually an approved course and there is an entire module specific to this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
sentences.text: The other thing I need to also highlight is that what we are doing in terms of security checks, as well as frisk searches, is not different, as I have said, from those that we have already been conducting for major public events, for instance, NDP.

sections.label: Vehicle forfeiture for illegal speed trials
sections.summary: The vehicle forfeiture regime for illegal speed trials is non-mandatory to be fair to non-consenting owners, though the Public Prosecutor can still apply for forfeiture.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: On the vehicle forfeiture regime for illegal speed trials, Mr Murali Pillai asked about the reason for making the vehicle forfeiture regime for illegal speed trials non-mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: While we want to deter persons from taking part in illegal speed trials through vehicle forfeiture, we also have to be fair to owners who did not consent to the offending driver using their vehicle and were not involved in the illegal speed trial.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: The Public Prosecutor still retains the power to apply for the forfeiture of a vehicle used in an illegal speed trial.

sections.label: Traffic enforcement camera network expansion
sections.summary: TP has stepped up enforcement and expanded its camera network, with close to 300 traffic enforcement cameras deployed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As I have mentioned in my opening speech, TP has stepped up enforcement and expanded its enforcement camera network to improve detection.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: There are now close to 300 traffic enforcement cameras deployed to detect and deter speeding and red light running.

sections.label: Broadened section 81 false information offence
sections.summary: Amendments broaden the section 81 offence to cover those who mislead TP and prevent identification of the correct driver, with fines doubled.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: To clarify, our proposed amendments to section 81 are not just increasing the penalties for the existing offence of furnishing false information.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We have broadened the offence to cover individuals who, alone or with others, deliberately mislead TP and prevent the identification of the correct offender driver.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Thus, we have increased the fine by two times to reflect the greater seriousness.

sections.label: Cyclist penalties and company responsible officer
sections.summary: A cyclist committing road rage hurt faces up to two years' imprisonment and a $5,000 fine, and companies must designate a responsible officer.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: For example, a cyclist who commits an offence of voluntarily causing hurt in a road rage type of incident will, similar to a motorist, be liable for a penalty of up to imprisonment of two years and a fine of $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We propose to amend the RTA to require companies to designate a responsible officer to see to the timely reporting of information needed for TP's investigation of the traffic incident.

sections.label: Fine deadlines and road safety culture
sections.summary: TP or LTA may extend traffic fine deadlines for meritorious financial difficulty appeals, and efforts go beyond enforcement to road safety culture.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Nevertheless, currently, for genuine cases of financial difficulty, if the individual appeals to TP or the LTA and the appeal is assessed to be meritorious, TP or LTA already extend their deadline to pay the traffic fine, by up to several months.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: This is probably even more helpful to the offender than an instalment plan.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Beyond the amendments to legislation, a wider change on building a good road safety culture is essential.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: Instead, there must be greater awareness, education and behavioural change." This is why our efforts have gone beyond enforcement, to encouraging a good road safety culture through engagement, education and infrastructural improvements.

sections.label: Enhanced penalties in Silver Zones
sections.summary: Motorists committing offences in Silver Zones will incur two additional demerit points and an additional $100 composition fine.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, we are going to enhance our penalties against irresponsible motorists in Silver Zones.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We want to encourage more and greater caution in areas which are frequented by elderly pedestrians.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We will be doing something shortly, later this year, where motorists who commit offences in the Silver Zones will incur two additional demerit points, on top of the usual demerit points.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: They will also be liable for an additional $100 in composition fine.
